name: Backlia – Backlinks & Content Distribution for SEO & AI Search
author: w3git

sections.description:
Backlia lets you distribute your own content across the Backlia network directly from the WordPress editor. When you publish a post and mark it for Backlia, the plugin sends the post’s URL, title and description to your Backlia account, which creates a public, indexable page for your content in the Backlia directory network — and that page links back to your post.

It is a content-distribution tool for your own website. It is not a link exchange, a private blog network, or a service that promises or manipulates search rankings.

Built for modern search: SEO, AEO and GEO

Search is no longer only about ten blue links. Backlia distributes your own content to additional indexable web pages, which can support your visibility across:

  • SEO (Search Engine Optimization) — traditional search engines that crawl and index the open web.
  • AEO (Answer Engine Optimization) — answer engines and assistants that read indexable pages to build responses.
  • GEO (Generative Engine Optimization) — generative/AI engines that cite and summarize publicly available web content.

Backlia does not make ranking promises. It simply makes your own content available on more indexable pages, with a backlink to the original post. Results depend on your content and the search engines themselves.

What you can do

  • Create a free Backlia account right from the plugin (email + password) — no separate signup needed.
  • On the free plan, generate 1 backlink for your own site’s domain. Need more backlinks, or backlinks for other domains? A paid plan is required.
  • Generate a backlink from any post with a single checkbox in the editor.
  • Optionally generate a backlink automatically for every new post you publish (toggle in Settings).
  • See all your backlinks in a dashboard inside wp-admin.
  • Choose a category/subcategory for each backlink (optional).

How it works

  1. Connect or create your Backlia account in Backlia → Settings.
  2. Edit any post. In the “Backlink” box (right column), tick “Generate a Backlia backlink” and adjust the title/description if you want.
  3. Publish or update the post. The backlink is created in the Backlia network (subject to your plan’s limit).

Languages

The plugin interface follows your WordPress language. It ships translated for Portuguese (Brazil), Spanish, French, German, Italian, Russian, Arabic, Japanese and Chinese (Simplified). If your WordPress is set to any other language, the interface is shown in English (US).

Account required

Backlia is a connected service. The plugin requires a free or paid Backlia account (created in seconds from the plugin) to work. Learn more at https://backlia.com/wordpress-plugin .

External services

This plugin connects to the Backlia service (https://backlia.com), operated by Backlia, to create and manage your account and your backlinks. This connection is required for the plugin to function.

When data is sent and what is sent:

  • Creating or connecting an account (when you submit the form in Backlia → Settings): your email address, your password (over HTTPS; the password is never stored by the plugin — only an access token is kept), and your site’s domain. In return the plugin receives an authentication token.
  • Publishing a post marked for Backlia: the post’s permalink (URL), title, description, and the optional category/subcategory you chose. In return the plugin receives the status of the created backlink.
  • Account/plan status, categories, and the embedded dashboard: the plugin loads your plan status, the list of categories, and a logged-in dashboard view from Backlia using your token.
  • Public post view counting: on a public post that you marked for Backlia, a small anonymous request is sent from the visitor’s browser to Backlia to count the backlink view. No personal data is sent; it only signals that the backlink was viewed.

No data is sent to Backlia until you connect/create an account and explicitly publish a post marked for Backlia.

  • Terms of Service: https://backlia.com/terms
  • Privacy Policy: https://backlia.com/privacy
sections.installation:
1. Install the plugin through Plugins → Add New, or upload the plugin zip via Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin.
  2. Activate the plugin.
  3. Go to Backlia → Settings and either create a free account (email + password) or connect your existing Backlia account.
  4. Edit a post, tick “Generate a Backlia backlink” in the Backlink box, and publish.
sections.faq:
Is it free?

Yes. After installing, you can create a free Backlia account and generate 1 backlink for your own site’s domain at no cost. More backlinks, or backlinks for other domains, require a paid plan.

Do I need a Backlia account?

Yes. You can create one for free in seconds, directly from the plugin’s Settings screen.

Does this guarantee better Google rankings?

No. Backlia distributes your own content to additional indexable pages and links back to your posts. It does not promise, sell or manipulate rankings. Search engines decide rankings on their own.

What are AEO and GEO?

AEO (Answer Engine Optimization) and GEO (Generative Engine Optimization) refer to being visible to answer engines and AI/generative engines that read publicly indexable web content. Backlia simply makes your content available on more indexable pages — it makes no guarantees about any engine.

Does the plugin send my password anywhere?

Your password is only used once, over HTTPS, to create or connect your account. The plugin stores only an access token — never your password.

Will it change or modify my posts?

No. The plugin reads the post’s URL, title and description to create a backlink. It does not alter your post content.

How do I create a backlink for every new post automatically?

In Backlia → Settings, enable “Generate a Backlia backlink automatically for all new posts”.

In which languages is the plugin available?

The UI follows your WordPress language: Portuguese (Brazil), Spanish, French, German, Italian, Russian, Arabic, Japanese and Chinese (Simplified) are bundled; any other language falls back to English (US).
sections.changelog:
1.4.3

  • Automation (auto-generate on all posts) now starts unchecked on activation; no auto-redirect after activating.

1.4.2

  • Plugin row links now point to the brand site (author opens in a new tab) and “About the plugin” points to the site.
  • Richer “View details” content (description, installation and FAQ).

1.4.0

  • Compliance and performance update: the dashboard and the Terms/Privacy links now open on backlia.com in a new tab (no embedded frames); all scripts and styles are properly enqueued; tidier admin menu placement; removed code that hid other plugins’ admin notices.

1.3.3

  • When a backlink is saved as inactive (Free plan, or your plan’s limit was reached), the editor now shows a modal explaining the reason, the release date and a link to subscribe/upgrade.

1.3.2

  • The “Add Backlink” posts screen also hides notices from other plugins/themes, showing only Backlia information.

1.3.1

  • The Backlia dashboard screen hides admin notices from other plugins/themes, keeping only Backlia information.

1.3.0

  • The Terms and Privacy Policy links on the Settings screen now open in a modal inside WordPress.

1.2.3

  • The embedded dashboard (All Backlinks) now follows your WordPress language.

1.2.2

  • Full English UI with internationalization (text domain) for the WordPress.org release.

1.2.1

  • WordPress.org release preparation: internationalization, English-first UI, updates handled by WordPress.org.

1.2.0

  • Create a free Backlia account directly from the plugin (1 free backlink for your own site).

1.1.0

  • Plan name, free-backlink counter and one-click activate/deactivate in the embedded dashboard; classic-editor support.
